title: URL Inspector
h1: URL Inspector — Parse Links into Parts
seoTitle: URL Inspector — Parse Links into Parts
description: Split a URL into protocol, host, port, path, query parameters and hash. Parsing stays in the browser and shows every query pair on its own line.
intro: Paste any absolute URL to see its pieces. Query parameters are decoded and listed so campaign links and API endpoints are easier to read.
blurb: Break an absolute URL into protocol, host, path, query pairs and hash.
howItWorks: The value is parsed with the browser URL constructor, so it must include a scheme.
Path, host, port and hash are read from the parsed object.
Each query parameter is decoded and listed; repeated keys stay as separate rows.
examples: https://example.com/docs?q=tool+nova shows q as tool nova.
A hash such as #install is reported separately from the path.
http://localhost:3000/api has host localhost and port 3000.

faq.a: Relative paths and missing schemes are not absolute URLs. Add https:// or http:// and try again.
No. It only parses the string locally and does not open the link.
